catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Structural, domain, and infrastructural architecture analysis of the Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner and knowledge repository.
analysis_limits: No direct runtime execution or network trace analysis; analysis is based on static manifest, tree structure, and symbol inspection.

system_map.overview: The Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner is structured as a multi-tier Python application pairing domain-driven architecture governance with a filesystem-based hierarchical knowledge base. It provides CLI operations, compliance checking, governance lifecycle state transitions, telemetry adaptation, and workspace bootstrapping.

layers.name: presentation
layers.purpose: CLI entrypoints and onboarding output formatting using Rich and command-line parsing.

layers.name: application
layers.purpose: Workflow execution orchestration, governance service coordination, and workspace bootstrapping.

layers.name: domain
layers.purpose: Core business models for governance entities, compliance findings, metrics, and health evaluation.

layers.name: infrastructure
layers.purpose: Third-party client adapters, telemetry normalization adapters, and file-system persistence access.

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Declares immutable and typed governance records, compliance metrics, and action states using Pydantic models.
patterns.intent: Ensure strict type validation, serialization consistency, and domain invariant enforcement across governance workflows.
patterns.context: Governance records, compliance findings, and action results must be passed across file boundaries, CLI commands, and metric dashboards.
forces: Data ingested from YAML and JSON files may have missing or malformed attributes.
Downstream consumers require guaranteed typings without scattered runtime type guards.
patterns.solution: Define data contracts as Pydantic models encapsulating governance inventories, compliance metrics, and resolution outputs.
implementation_signals: Structured dataclasses representing domain outputs like ComplianceFinding and GovernanceAction

evidence.note: Complete domain boundary defined using structured Pydantic models.

benefits: Automatic schema validation and serialization to JSON/dict formats.
Clear boundary definitions between external serialized formats and domain entities.
costs: Runtime validation overhead during high-volume object instantiation.
failure_modes: Schema divergence between raw Markdown/YAML frontmatter and Pydantic validation rules leading to parse exceptions.

patterns.name: Adapter Telemetry Normalization
patterns.summary: Normalizes disparate tracing formats into a canonical AgentTelemetrySpan domain record using targeted adapter classes.
patterns.intent: Isolate external vendor-specific trace formats from internal dashboards and health calculation models.
patterns.context: Agent and developer interactions generate telemetry spans from diverse environments (e.g. Claude Code, Antigravity) that must be ingested uniformly.
forces: Heterogeneous payload structures and timestamp representations across tracing providers.
Core metric dashboards should not depend on vendor-specific span schemas.
patterns.solution: Implement provider-specific adapters (CodingAgentTelemetryAdapter, AntigravityTelemetryAdapter, ClaudeCodeTelemetryAdapter) inheriting from a common interface to convert raw data into AgentTelemetrySpan instances.

evidence.note: Specialized adapter implementations mapping third-party spans into a single canonical telemetry model.

benefits: Pluggable support for new telemetry emitters without modifying the dashboard or health models.
Encapsulated timestamp normalization and cost attribution logic.
costs: Duplicate mapping logic across adapters when schema structures slightly diverge.
failure_modes: Provider trace schema updates silent failures defaulting to unrecognized provider tags.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Manages valid state transitions and governance progression through an explicit transition registry table.
patterns.intent: Prevent invalid status transitions in governance artifacts and enforce deterministic life-cycle progression.
patterns.context: Governance actions, decision records, and architectural work items progress through discrete review and promotion stages.
forces: Ad-hoc status modification leads to orphaned or inconsistently approved governance records.
Decoupling the transition validation logic from execution engines.
patterns.solution: Define a TransitionRegistry that holds verified valid state transitions, invoked by GovernanceActionEngine prior to mutations.
implementation_signals: Explicit registry object checking source and target states
Separation between transition verification and engine execution

evidence.note: TransitionRegistry encapsulates permitted transition paths enforced by GovernanceActionEngine.

benefits: Centralized rule set for valid lifecycle paths.
Simplified testing of permissible states without running external actions.
costs: New lifecycle states require updating registry mappings before usage.
failure_modes: Unregistered edge cases causing valid actions to be blocked by rigid transition definitions.

patterns.name: Service Layer Governance Orchestration
patterns.summary: Encapsulates application workflow orchestration into a dedicated service layer behind the CLI boundary.
patterns.intent: Coordinate domain actions, compliance checks, and state transitions without leaking presentation logic into domain engines.
patterns.context: The CLI needs to invoke governance checks, state transitions, and metrics computation in unified command flows.
forces: CLI handlers risk becoming bloated with business logic if they manage domain rules directly.
Multiple consumers (CLI, CI/CD runners, future APIs) need identical orchestration guarantees.
patterns.solution: Introduce GovernanceActionService to orchestrate calls between TransitionRegistry, ComplianceEngine, and domain models.
implementation_signals: CLI delegating directly to high-level service methods

evidence.note: Dedicated service coordinating governance actions and reporting.
Presentation entrypoint delegating orchestration duties to application services.

benefits: Clean separation of CLI arguments handling from domain execution flow.
Reusable application service suitable for programmatic calls from testing or automation scripts.
costs: Additional indirection layer for straightforward operations.
failure_modes: Service layer accumulating unrelated orchestration responsibilities over time.

patterns.name: Swappable Client Adapter
patterns.summary: Decouples LLM and provider invocation through matching client abstractions, providing both live and mock implementations.
patterns.intent: Enable offline testing and zero-cost local verification without relying on external remote network clients.
patterns.context: Components requiring model evaluations need deterministic offline execution during unit testing and CI builds.
forces: External model API calls introduce non-determinism, latency, and cost to local CI runs.
Domain engines should not bind directly to litellm library primitives.
patterns.solution: Provide parallel LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient adhering to uniform invocation semantics.
implementation_signals: Parallel client classes under llm package
Mock client capable of satisfying client calls without network interaction

evidence.note: Production implementation targeting the LiteLLM library.
Mock implementation allowing local unit testing and offline execution.

benefits: High testability in CI environments without API keys or external dependencies.
Direct isolation of provider payload changes.
costs: Mock client must be maintained to keep parity with live client interfaces.
failure_modes: Behavior drift between MockLLMClient and LiteLLMClient causing false-positive test passes.

patterns.name: Filesystem Hierarchical Knowledge Store
patterns.summary: Organizes architecture governance artifacts in a partitioned markdown/YAML directory hierarchy separating global, project, and runtime scopes.
patterns.intent: Use Git-trackable files to store architectural decisions, narratives, maps, and rules without requiring an external database.
patterns.context: Architecture specifications, ADRs, and compliance rules must be versioned, reviewed via pull requests, and accessible locally.
forces: Developers and architects work in Git repositories; external documentation databases break change tracking.
Need clean separation between global organization-wide rules and project-specific variations.
patterns.solution: Structure the repository into explicit folders: `cas-knowledge/global/` (decisions, governance, maps, models, narratives, patterns, rules, signals), `cas-knowledge/projects/`, and `cas-knowledge/runtime/`.
implementation_signals: Directory partitioned by scope: global/, projects/, runtime/, templates/
Markdown templates for decisions, patterns, rules, and signals

evidence.note: Directory structure partitioning global, project, runtime, and template governance data.

benefits: Version-controlled knowledge base with full Git audit trail and PR review workflows.
Human-readable Markdown/YAML documentation directly co-located with code.
costs: Query operations require directory scans and file parsing rather than indexed lookups.
failure_modes: Broken relative links and naming divergences between project directories.

patterns.name: Symlink Workspace Projection
patterns.summary: Initializes and updates local consumer repositories by projecting governance rules and agent configurations via symlink or deep merge.
patterns.intent: Ensure client workspaces retain synchronized governance configurations and skill definitions without copy-paste drift.
patterns.context: Downstream repositories need standardized CAS configurations (e.g. Claude settings, agent rules, and templates) anchored to centralized standards.
forces: Manual distribution of governance files leads to drift across multiple development workspaces.
Operating systems without symlink support require fallback file copying.
patterns.solution: Implement a bootstrap mechanism (_create_symlink_or_copy, merge_claude_settings, merge_cas_governance_block) that projects configuration into local workspaces.
implementation_signals: Fallback helper from symlink to copy on failure
JSON/YAML merge functions preserving local configurations while updating managed blocks

evidence.note: Workspace initialization procedures orchestrating file links and configuration merges.

benefits: Centralized updates propagate automatically to projects linking back to the core repository.
Preserves project-specific customizations via block-based merging.
costs: Filesystem permission issues or broken links on Windows/containerized environments.
failure_modes: Overwriting uncommitted local changes if merge logic misinterprets custom blocks.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Filesystem Scanning
symptoms: Compliance checks and telemetry lookups recursively scanning directories without depth bounds or caching.
impact: Degraded CLI execution performance as knowledge repositories grow to hundreds of projects and files.
suggested_remediation: Introduce indexed metadata caches or pre-computed manifest indices to minimize direct disk hits.

anti_patterns.name: Dual Configuration Settings Sync Drift
symptoms: Separate directories maintaining parallel agent configs (e.g., `.agents/` vs `.claude/`).
impact: Configuration drift when skill definitions or subagent instructions are updated in one provider folder but not the other.
suggested_remediation: Maintain a single canonical skill source and generate provider-specific directories via build tasks.

cross_cutting_concerns.description: Utilizes OpenTelemetry SDK to track spans and cost metrics across governance checks and telemetry ingest flows.
Uses jsonschema and Pydantic models to validate configurations and governance artifacts across runtime boundaries.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent modifications to cas-knowledge files prevented when multiple CI runners execute governance checks simultaneously?
open_questions.context: The knowledge base relies on local disk read/writes without evidence of distributed lock management.
